## Tek kelimelik bir yemin

[¶1] Sure tek bir kelimeyle açılır: {ar:وَٱلْعَصْرِ, tr:ve'l-asr, gloss:asra andolsun, source:103:1}. Baştaki "ve" burada iki şeyi birbirine bağlayan bağlaç değil, yemin edatıdır; ardındaki isim bu yüzden esre ile okunur. Yeminin neye dair olduğu bu ayette söylenmez, bir sonraki ayete bırakılır. Birinci ayet bu yüzden bir eşik gibidir: okuyan, neyin üzerine yemin edildiğini duyar, ama hangi hükmün söyleneceğini henüz bilmez. Hüküm ikinci ayette gelir: {ar:إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ, tr:inne'l-insâne le-fî husr, gloss:insan gerçekten kayıp içindedir, source:103:2}. Yeminle öne konan şey, ardından gelecek hükmün hemen yanına yerleştirilmiştir; asrın ne olduğunu iyi duymak, kaybın nasıl bir kayıp olduğunu duymanın da yoludur.

[¶2] Kur'an başka surelerde de günün vakitleri üzerine yemin eder: {ar:وَٱلْفَجْرِ, tr:ve'l-fecr, gloss:şafağa andolsun, source:89:1}, {ar:وَٱلضُّحَىٰ, tr:ve'd-duhâ, gloss:kuşluk vaktine andolsun, source:93:1}, {ar:وَٱلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ, tr:ve'l-leyli izâ yağşâ, gloss:her şeyi örttüğünde geceye andolsun, source:92:1}, {ar:وَٱلصُّبْحِ إِذَآ أَسْفَرَ, tr:ve's-subhi izâ esfer, gloss:ağardığında sabaha andolsun, source:74:34}. Bunların çoğunda vakit bir hareketle birlikte anılır: gece örttüğünde, sabah ağardığında. Asr ise yalnız gelir, hiçbir niteleme almaz; bu yalnızlık kelimenin genişliğini açık bırakır. Çünkü aynı kelime hem günün bir dilimini hem de zamanın bütününü adlandırır. Uzun zamana, çağa {ar:العصر الدهر, tr:el-asru'd-dehr, gloss:asr, uzun zaman, çağdır, source:"ع ص ر,B001"} denir; günün akşama yakın kısmına da {ar:العصر العشي, tr:el-asru'l-aşiyy, gloss:asr, akşamüstüdür, source:"ع ص ر,B001"}; o vakitte kılınan namaz da adını ondan alır: {ar:صلاة العصر, tr:salâtu'l-asr, gloss:ikindi namazı, source:"ع ص ر,B001"}. Kelimedeki belirlilik takısı bilinen bir vakti gösterir, ama hangisinin, günün ikindisinin mi, insanın içinde yaşadığı çağın mı, zamanın kendisinin mi kastedildiğini ayet söylemez. Tek kelime, okuyanı bunları birlikte duymaya bırakır.

[¶3] Türkçe bu kelimeyi ikiye bölmüştür. "Asır" bugün yüz yıl demektir, "asri" de çağdaş; günün sonu ise "ikindi" diye başka bir kelimeyle söylenir. Türkçede "asır" denince ne akşamüstünün azalan ışığı duyulur ne de aşağıda görülecek sıkma, sığınak ve kasırga. Ayetteki kelime ise saati de çağı da bir arada tutar: bir günün sonu ile bir ömrün sonu aynı adı taşır.

[¶4] Araplar kelimeyi ikil olarak da kullanır, günün iki ucunu birlikte "iki asr" diye anarlardı: {ar:العصران الليل والنهار, tr:el-asrâni'l-leylu ve'n-nehâr, gloss:iki asr, gece ile gündüz, source:"ع ص ر,B001"}, {ar:العصران الغداة والعشي, tr:el-asrâni'l-gadâtu ve'l-aşiyy, gloss:iki asr, sabah erkeni ile akşamüstü, source:"ع ص ر,B001"}. Kur'an bu çifti, günün iki kenarını, kendi sözleriyle anar. Peygamber'e, yanındaki bir grup mümin hakkında şöyle denir: {ar:وَلَا تَطْرُدِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَدَوٰةِ وَٱلْعَشِىِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُۥ, tr:ve lâ tatrudi'llezîne yed'ûne rabbehum bi'l-gadâti ve'l-aşiyyi yurîdûne vechehû, gloss:sabah akşam, O'nun rızasını isteyerek Rablerine yalvaranları kovma, source:6:52}. Bir başka surede, dosdoğru durması emredilen Peygamber'e namazın vakti yine bu iki uçla verilir: {ar:وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ طَرَفَىِ ٱلنَّهَارِ وَزُلَفًۭا مِّنَ ٱلَّيْلِ, tr:ve ekimi's-salâte tarafeyi'n-nehâri ve zulefen mine'l-leyl, gloss:namazı gündüzün iki ucunda ve gecenin ilk saatlerinde kıl, source:11:114}. Asrın günün iki ucunun adı olması, kelimenin zamanı kenarından tuttuğunu gösterir: bir dönemin girildiği ve çıkıldığı yerden. Ayetin akşamüstü anlamı da bu kenarlardan biridir, günün kapanan ucu.

## Geç gelen ve kısalan vakit

[¶5] Kelime gecikmeyi de taşır. Biri vaktinden sonra, ağır ağır gelince {ar:جاءني فلان عصرا أي بطيئا, tr:câenî fulânun asran, gloss:falanca bana geç, ağır ağır geldi, source:"ع ص ر,B001"} derlerdi. Gözüne uyku girmemiş biri için {ar:نام وما نام لعصر, tr:nâme ve mâ nâme li-asr, gloss:yattı ama bir an bile uyumadı, source:"ع ص ر,B001"} denirdi; bir zaman parçasına {ar:العصار الحين, tr:el-asâru'l-hîn, gloss:asâr, bir süredir, source:"ع ص ر,B001"} adı verilirdi. Böylece asr hem uzun bir çağdır hem de göz açıp kapayıncaya kadar geçen an; hem günün olağan bir dilimidir hem de gecikmiş gelişin vakti. Bir insan ömrünün evrelerine de aynı kelimeyle işaret edilir: genç kız için {ar:بلغت عصر شبابها وإدراكها, tr:belegat asra şebâbihâ ve idrâkihâ, gloss:gençliğinin ve erginliğinin çağına erdi, source:"ع ص ر,B009"} derler, kişinin ömrü ve yaşlılığı da bu adla anılır {source:"ع ص ر,B001"}. Akşamüstü günün kalanının en az olduğu saattir: iş bitmek üzeredir, ışık azalır, yapılmamış olan için vakit daralır. Asr bu yüzden yalnızca bir saat değil, bir saatin içinde duyulan geç kalmışlıktır.

[¶6] Kur'an zamanın sonda nasıl daraldığını, insanın kendi süresini dönüp nasıl ölçtüğünü gösterir. Peygamber'e kıyamet sorulur: {ar:يَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلسَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرْسَىٰهَا, tr:yes'elûneke ani's-sâ'ati eyyâne mursâhâ, gloss:sana o Saat'i, ne zaman demir atacağını soruyorlar, source:79:42}. Surenin son ayeti cevap yerine bir ölçü verir; o Saat görüldüğünde bütün ömür bir günün tek dilimine iner: {ar:كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَهَا لَمْ يَلْبَثُوٓا۟ إِلَّا عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَىٰهَا, tr:keennehum yevme yerevnehâ lem yelbesû illâ aşiyyeten ev duhâhâ, gloss:onu gördükleri gün, sanki bir akşamüstü ya da onun kuşluğu kadar kalmışlardır, source:79:46}. Buradaki kelime asr değildir, ama asrın kendisiyle açıklandığı akşamüstüdür: uzun çağ ile akşamüstünün aynı kelimede durması, sondan bakılınca birinin ötekine dönüşmesidir. Cehennemdekilerin feryadında ise geç kalmış iş açıkça görünür: {ar:رَبَّنَآ أَخْرِجْنَا نَعْمَلْ صَٰلِحًا غَيْرَ ٱلَّذِى كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ, tr:rabbenâ ahricnâ na'mel sâlihan gayra'llezî kunnâ na'mel, gloss:Rabbimiz, bizi çıkar da yaptığımızdan başka, salih bir iş yapalım, source:35:37}; aynı ayetteki cevap ömrü verilmiş bir süre olarak anar: {ar:أَوَلَمْ نُعَمِّرْكُم مَّا يَتَذَكَّرُ فِيهِ مَن تَذَكَّرَ, tr:e-ve lem nu'ammirkum mâ yetezekkeru fîhi men tezekker, gloss:size, düşünecek olanın düşünebileceği kadar ömür vermedik mi, source:35:37}. İkinci ayetin kaybı da, üçüncü ayetin iman ve salih işi de bu verilmiş süre içinde yer alır.

## Sıkmak: öz, kuruluk ve yudum

[¶7] Kelimenin en somut işi sıkmaktır. Buradan sonra anılacak imgeler ayetteki "zaman" anlamının yerine geçmez, onun yanında duyulur. Sıkma bir yöntemle tarif edilir: {ar:ضغط شيء حتى يتحلب, tr:dagtu şey'in hattâ yetehalleb, gloss:bir şeyi suyu sağılır gibi akana dek bastırmak, source:"ع ص ر,B002"}. Üzüm sıkmak için yem torbasına benzeyen bir torba kullanılırdı: {ar:المعصار شيء كالمخلاة يجعل فيه العنب ويعصر, tr:el-mi'sâr şey'un ke'l-mihlât, gloss:içine üzüm konup sıkılan, yem torbasına benzer bir şey, source:"ع ص ر,B002"}; sıkmanın yapıldığı yere de {ar:المعصرة ما يعصر فيه العنب, tr:el-ma'sara, gloss:içinde üzüm sıkılan yer, source:"ع ص ر,B002"} denirdi. Torba üzümü bir arada tutar, el ya da ağırlık onu bastırır, kabuklar yarılır ve sıvı torbanın dokusundan süzülüp akar. Akana {ar:العصارة ما سال عن العصر, tr:el-usâratu mâ sâle ani'l-asr, gloss:usâre, sıkmadan akandır, source:"ع ص ر,B002"} adı verilir; suyu sıkılarak alınmış her şeye de {ar:كل شيء عصر ماؤه فهو عصير, tr:kullu şey'in usira mâuhû fe-huve asîr, gloss:suyu sıkılmış her şey asîrdir, source:"ع ص ر,B002"} denir. Torbada kalan ise posadır {source:"ع ص ر,B002"}. Sıkma böylece bir şeyi ikiye ayırır: akıp giden öz ve geride kalan kuru kütle.

[¶8] Bu işin ürünü iyiliğin adı olmuştur. Araplar sıkılıp akan özü hayrın ve bağışın misali yaparlardı {ar:العرب تجعل العصارة والمعتصر مثلا للخير والعطاء, tr:el-arabu tec'alu'l-usârate ve'l-mu'tasare mesalen li'l-hayri ve'l-atâ', gloss:Araplar usâreyi ve sıkılan yeri hayır ve bağış için misal yaparlar, source:"ع ص ر,B007"}; cömert biri için {ar:يعصر فينا كالذي تعصر, tr:ya'siru fînâ ke'llezî ta'sir, gloss:bize senin verdiğin gibi verir, source:"ع ص ر,B007"} derlerdi, topraktan alınan gelire de {ar:العصارة الغلة, tr:el-usâratu'l-galle, gloss:usâre, üründür, source:"ع ص ر,B007"} denirdi. Sıkma göğe de taşınır. Bulutun yağmurla sıkıldığı söylenir: {ar:المعصرات السحائب تعتصر بالمطر, tr:el-mu'sırâtu's-sehâibu ta'tasıru bi'l-matar, gloss:mu'sırât, yağmurla sıkılan bulutlardır, source:"ع ص ر,B003"}, {ar:السحابة المعصر التي تتحلب بالمطر, tr:es-sehâbetu'l-mu'sır, gloss:yağmuru sağılır gibi akıtan bulut, source:"ع ص ر,B003"}; yağmura kavuşan topluluk için {ar:عصر القوم أي مطروا, tr:usira'l-kavm, gloss:topluluk yağmura kavuştu, source:"ع ص ر,B003"} denir. Kur'an bu bulutları kendi adlarıyla anar. Kıyamet haberini tartışanlara yeryüzünün düzeni sayılırken şöyle denir: {ar:وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمُعْصِرَٰتِ مَآءًۭ ثَجَّاجًۭا, tr:ve enzelnâ mine'l-mu'sırâti mâen seccâcâ, gloss:sıkılan bulutlardan şarıl şarıl su indirdik, source:78:14}, {ar:لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِۦ حَبًّۭا وَنَبَاتًۭا, tr:li-nuhrice bihî habben ve nebâtâ, gloss:onunla tane ve bitki çıkaralım diye, source:78:15}, {ar:وَجَنَّٰتٍ أَلْفَافًا, tr:ve cennâtin elfâfâ, gloss:ve iç içe geçmiş bahçeler, source:78:16}. Bulutun sıkılması burada bir bereket zinciri başlatır: sıkılan bulut, tane, bitki, bahçe.

[¶9] Sıkmanın öteki ucu kuruluktur. Susuzluktan kurumuş dile {ar:المعصور اللسان اليابس عطشا, tr:el-ma'sûru'l-lisânu'l-yâbisu atşâ, gloss:ma'sûr, susuzluktan kurumuş dildir, source:"ع ص ر,B014"} denir: sıkılmış, içinde su kalmamış dil. Aynı fiil bir kurtuluş hareketini de adlandırır. Lokma boğazına takılan kişi suyu azar azar içerek onu geçirir: {ar:الاعتصار أن يغص الإنسان بالطعام فيعتصر بالماء وهو أن يشربه قليلا قليلا ليسيغه, tr:el-i'tisâru en yagassa'l-insânu bi't-taâmi fe-ya'tasıra bi'l-mâ', gloss:i'tisâr, insanın yemekle tıkanınca suyu yudum yudum içip lokmayı geçirmesidir, source:"ع ص ر,B008"}. Bir şair bu hareketi tersinden kullanmıştır: {ar:لو بغير الماء حلقي شرق كنت كالغصان بالماء اعتصاري, tr:lev bi-gayri'l-mâi halkî şarikun kuntu ke'l-gassâni bi'l-mâi'-tisârî, gloss:boğazım sudan başka bir şeyle tıkansaydı, suyla yudumlayıp kurtulan tıkanmış biri gibi olurdum, source:"ع ص ر,B008"}; söylemediği ama duyurduğu şudur: onu tıkayan suyun kendisidir, kurtaracak yudum kalmamıştır.

[¶10] Bu imgeler ayetteki zamanın yanında duyulunca zaman bir baskı olarak görünür. Günler insanın üzerinden geçer ve ondan bir şey çıkarır: ya özü akar, bağış olur, bulut gibi yağmur bırakır, ya da kuru bir kütle, susuzluktan kurumuş bir dil kalır. İkinci ayetteki kayıp, sıkılmış olanın geride kalan yanıdır; üçüncü ayetin son kelimesi olan sabrın da bir ağaçtan sıkılan acı özün adı olması {source:"ص ب ر,B008"} bu baskıyı surenin sonuna taşır.

## Yusuf'un zindanında sıkılan üzüm ve beklenen yıl

[¶11] Kur'an sıkma fiilini bir zindanda kullanır ve onu uzun bir bekleyişin içine yerleştirir. Yusuf suçsuz olduğu belli olduktan sonra, kendisini sıkıştıranların kararıyla zindana atılır: {ar:لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُۥ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍۢ, tr:le-yescununnehû hattâ hîn, gloss:onu bir süreye kadar mutlaka zindana atacaklardı, source:12:35}. Zindan burada bir süre ile ölçülmüştür; asra da bir zaman parçası denildiğini, kelimenin alıkoymak anlamı da taşıdığını hatırlamak gerekir {source:"ع ص ر,B006"}. Bu bir bağlantıdır, kelime ortaklığı değil: Kur'an zindan için başka bir kelime kullanır. Yusuf'la birlikte zindana iki genç girer; biri rüyasını anlatır: {ar:إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰنِىٓ أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًۭا, tr:innî erânî a'siru hamrâ, gloss:kendimi şarap sıkarken görüyorum, source:12:36}. Gencin sıktığı şey üzümdür, ama cümle onu çıkacak içkinin adıyla söyler: sıkma, ürününün adıyla anılır. Yusuf'un yorumu bu genç için kurtuluştur: {ar:أَمَّآ أَحَدُكُمَا فَيَسْقِى رَبَّهُۥ خَمْرًۭا, tr:emmâ ehadukumâ fe-yeskî rabbehû hamrâ, gloss:biriniz efendisine şarap sunacak, source:12:41}. Ardından gelen ayet onu kurtulacak olan diye anar: {ar:وَقَالَ لِلَّذِى ظَنَّ أَنَّهُۥ نَاجٍۢ مِّنْهُمَا ٱذْكُرْنِى عِندَ رَبِّكَ, tr:ve kâle li'llezî zanne ennehû nâcin minhumâ'zkurnî inde rabbik, gloss:ikisinden kurtulacağını sandığına: beni efendinin yanında an, dedi, source:12:42}. Asrın kurtuluş yeri anlamına da {ar:العصر المنجاة, tr:el-asru'l-mencât, gloss:asr, kurtuluş yeridir, source:"ع ص ر,B005"} denmesi bu sahnede yankılanır: rüyasında sıkan, zindandan kurtulan kişidir.

[¶12] Ama aynı ayet bekleyişi de uzatır: genç Yusuf'u anmayı unutur ve {ar:فَلَبِثَ فِى ٱلسِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ, tr:fe-lebise fi's-sicni bid'a sinîn, gloss:Yusuf zindanda birkaç yıl kaldı, source:12:42}. Unutan genç ancak kralın rüyası anlatıldığında hatırlar: {ar:وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِى نَجَا مِنْهُمَا وَٱدَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ, tr:ve kâle'llezî necâ minhumâ veddekera ba'de ummeh, gloss:ikisinden kurtulmuş olan, uzun bir süre sonra hatırlayıp dedi, source:12:45}. Kralın rüyasında yedi yeşil başak ve yedi kuru başak vardır {ar:وَسَبْعَ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍۢ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍۢ, tr:ve seb'a sunbulâtin hudrin ve uhara yâbisât, gloss:yedi yeşil başak ve ötekiler kuru, source:12:43}. Yusuf'un yorumu bir zaman planıdır. Önce yedi yıl ekilecek ve ürün başağında bırakılacaktır: {ar:فَمَا حَصَدتُّمْ فَذَرُوهُ فِى سُنۢبُلِهِۦٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا مِّمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ, tr:fe-mâ hasadtum fe-zerûhu fî sunbulihî illâ kalîlen mimmâ te'kulûn, gloss:biçtiğinizi, yiyeceğiniz az bir kısım dışında başağında bırakın, source:12:47}. Araplar, başağın kabukları belirdiğinde ekin için {ar:إذا تبينت أكمام السنبل قيل قد عصر الزرع, tr:izâ tebeyyenet ekmâmu's-sunbuli kîle kad asara'z-zer', gloss:başağın kabukları belirince ekin "asara" oldu denir, source:"ع ص ر,B010"} derlerdi ve bunu korunak anlamına bağlarlardı: {ar:مأخوذ من العصر وهو الحرز أي تحرز في غلفه, tr:me'hûzun mine'l-asri ve huve'l-hirz, gloss:korunak anlamındaki asrdan alınmıştır, tane kabuğunun içinde korunur, source:"ع ص ر,B010"}. Bu bir kalıp içinde yaşayan anlamdır ve Kur'an'ın kelimesi başaktır, asr değil; ama Yusuf'un planı tam bu işi yapar: tane, kabuğunun içinde, darlık yıllarına saklanır. Sonra yedi sert yıl gelir ve saklananı yer: {ar:ثُمَّ يَأْتِى مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ سَبْعٌۭ شِدَادٌۭ يَأْكُلْنَ مَا قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا مِّمَّا تُحْصِنُونَ, tr:summe ye'tî min ba'di zâlike seb'un şidâdun ye'kulne mâ kaddemtum lehunne illâ kalîlen mimmâ tuhsınûn, gloss:sonra yedi çetin yıl gelir, onlar için biriktirdiğinizi yer, koruyup sakladığınız az bir kısım kalır, source:12:48}. Ve en sonunda: {ar:ثُمَّ يَأْتِى مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ عَامٌۭ فِيهِ يُغَاثُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَفِيهِ يَعْصِرُونَ, tr:summe ye'tî min ba'di zâlike âmun fîhi yugâsu'n-nâsu ve fîhi ya'sirûn, gloss:sonra bir yıl gelir; o yıl insanlar imdada kavuşur ve o yıl sıkarlar, source:12:49}. Bu son fiil, topraktan ürün almak diye de anlaşılmıştır: {ar:يعصرون قال يستغلون بأرضيهم, tr:ya'sirûn, yestagıllûne bi-aradîhim, gloss:sıkarlar, yani topraklarından ürün alırlar, source:"ع ص ر,B007"}.

[¶13] Bu hikâyede kökün birbirinden uzak görünen anlamları tek bir takvime dizilir: zindanda geçen süre, kurtulacak olanın rüyasındaki sıkma, unutulup uzayan yıllar, kabuğunda saklanan tane ve sıkmanın yeniden başladığı bolluk yılı. Sıkmak burada darlığın sonunu işaret eder; sıkılacak üzüm, darlık yıllarını sabırla bekleyip saklayanların payıdır. Ayetin yemin ettiği zaman bu açıdan yalnızca tüketen bir süre değildir: içinde saklananın korunduğu ve sonunda sıkılıp akan bir süredir.

## Tutmak ve vermek

[¶14] Sıkmak bir kavrayıştır, ve kavrayış iki yöne işler: tutar ya da akıtır. Asr kelimesi tutmayı da adlandırır: {ar:العصر الحبس, tr:el-asru'l-habs, gloss:asr, alıkoymaktır, source:"ع ص ر,B006"}; birine seni ne alıkoydu diye sorulurken {ar:ما عصرك أي ما منعك, tr:mâ asarak, gloss:seni ne tuttu, ne engelledi, source:"ع ص ر,B006"} denirdi. Elinden bir şey bırakmayan, veremeyen kişi için {ar:فلان عاصر إذا كان ممسكا, tr:fulânun âsirun izâ kâne mumsikâ, gloss:eli sıkı olana âsir denir, source:"ع ص ر,B006"} derlerdi. Babanın, çocuğuna ait malı ondan tutması da bu fiille söylenir: {ar:يعتصر الوالد على ولده في ماله أي يمنعه إياه ويحبسه عنه, tr:ya'tasıru'l-vâlidu alâ veledihî fî mâlih, gloss:baba çocuğunun malını ondan esirger, alıkoyar, source:"ع ص ر,B006"}; verdiği bağıştan dönüp onu geri almak da: {ar:أعطيت فلانا عطية فاعتصرتها أي رجعت فيها, tr:a'taytu fulânen atıyyeten fa'tasartuhâ, gloss:birine bir bağış verdim, sonra ondan dönüp geri aldım, source:"ع ص ر,B006"}. Bir önceki bölümdeki cömert ise aynı kökle {source:"ع ص ر,B007"} verendi. Torba örneği bu ikiliği açıklar: sıkan el sıkıca kavrar; kavrayış sıvıyı dışarı akıtırsa bağış olur, kavrayış yalnızca tutarsa cimrilik olur. Aynı fiil hem el açıklığını hem el sıkılığını adlandırabilir, çünkü ikisi de bir şeyi avuçta sıkmaktır; fark, avuçtan bir şeyin çıkıp çıkmamasıdır.

[¶15] Tutmak her zaman kötü değildir. İlk aybaşı vaktinde evde tutulan genç kızın adı da buradan gelir: {ar:المعصر ساعة تطمث أي تحيض لأنها تحبس في البيت يجعل لها عصرا, tr:el-mu'sır, gloss:ilk aybaşı vaktindeki kız; evde tutulduğu, kendisine bir korunak yapıldığı için böyle denir, source:"ع ص ر,B009"}; kabuğunda saklanan tane de aynı korunağın içindedir {source:"ع ص ر,B010"}. Burada tutmak, bir eşikte olanı korumaktır.

[¶16] Kur'an ürünü tutmanın ne getirdiğini bir bahçe sahneleriyle anlatır. Peygamber'i yalanlayanlara, onları bir bahçenin sahipleri gibi sınadığını söyler: {ar:إِنَّا بَلَوْنَٰهُمْ كَمَا بَلَوْنَآ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ إِذْ أَقْسَمُوا۟ لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِينَ, tr:innâ belevnâhum kemâ belevnâ ashâbe'l-cenneti iz aksemû le-yasrimunnehâ musbihîn, gloss:onları, sabah olunca bahçenin ürününü mutlaka devşireceklerine yemin eden bahçe sahiplerini sınadığımız gibi sınadık, source:68:17}, {ar:وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ, tr:ve lâ yestesnûn, gloss:ve hiçbir istisna yapmıyorlardı, source:68:18}. Niyetleri, ürünü yoksula kapatmaktır: {ar:أَن لَّا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُم مِّسْكِينٌۭ, tr:en lâ yedhulennehe'l-yevme aleykum miskîn, gloss:bugün oraya yanınıza hiçbir yoksul girmesin, source:68:24}. Onlar uyurken bahçenin üzerinden Rab'den gelen bir şey geçer {ar:فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَآئِفٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمْ نَآئِمُونَ, tr:fe-tâfe aleyhâ tâifun min rabbike ve hum nâimûn, gloss:onlar uyurken Rabbinden bir dolaşan onun üzerinden dolaştı, source:68:19} ve bahçe kopkoyu bir yere döner {ar:فَأَصْبَحَتْ كَٱلصَّرِيمِ, tr:fe-asbahat ke's-sarîm, gloss:sabaha kesilip kararmış gibi çıktı, source:68:20}. Gördüklerinde ilk sözleri {ar:إِنَّا لَضَآلُّونَ, tr:innâ le-dâllûn, gloss:biz yolu şaşırmışız, source:68:26}, ardından {ar:بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ, tr:bel nahnu mahrûmûn, gloss:hayır, biz yoksun bırakılmışız, source:68:27} olur. Tutulan ürün tutanın elinde kalmamıştır. Bu bahçe sahipleri istisnasız bir yemin etmişlerdi; surenin yemini ise ikinci ayetteki genel hükmün ardından üçüncü ayetin istisnasıyla tamamlanır.

[¶17] Asrın sıkıştırma anlamının karşısında, şaşırtıcı biçimde, sığınak anlamı durur. Kök tutunmayı anlatır: {ar:تعلق بشيء وامتساك به, tr:teallukun bi-şey'in ve imtisâkun bih, gloss:bir şeye asılmak ve ona sıkıca tutunmak, source:"ع ص ر,B005"}. Tutunulan yerin adı da asrdır: {ar:العصر الملجأ, tr:el-asru'l-melce', gloss:asr, sığınaktır, source:"ع ص ر,B005"}; birine sığınan {ar:اعتصرت بفلان وتعصرت أي التجأت إليه, tr:i'tasartu bi-fulânin ve teassartu, gloss:falancaya sığındım, source:"ع ص ر,B005"} derdi, bir yere sığınan için de {ar:اعتصر بالمكان إذا التجأ إليه, tr:i'tasara bi'l-mekân, gloss:o yere sığındı, source:"ع ص ر,B005"} denirdi. İki insan arasındaki bağ da bu kelimeyle, olmayışıyla anılır: {ar:ما بينهما عصر ولا يصر أي ما بينهما مودة ولا قرابة, tr:mâ beynehumâ asrun ve lâ yasr, gloss:aralarında ne sevgi ne akrabalık var, source:"ع ص ر,B005"}. [¶18] Aynı kelimenin hem sıkıştırmayı hem sığınağı adlandırması ilk bakışta çelişki gibi görünür, ama ikisi de bir kavrayıştır. Sıkma bir şeyi dışarıdan sarar; sığınan ise kendisi bir şeyi sıkıca kavrar, zırh da bedeni dışarıdan sarar ve korur. Sıkışmış olan, bunalmış olan sığınağa koşar: deyimdeki sığınak tam da bunalmış kişinin sığınağıdır. Bu imge zamanın yanında duyulunca yemin edilen vakit hem insanı sıkıştıran bir süre hem de sığınılacak bir yer olarak görünür.

[¶19] Kur'an bir sığınağın zamanı nasıl kapattığını bir mağara hikâyesinde gösterir. Allah Peygamber'e, kavimlerinin taptıklarından ayrılan birkaç gencin haberini anlatır; onlar birbirine şöyle der: {ar:وَإِذِ ٱعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ فَأْوُۥٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ يَنشُرْ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُم مِّن رَّحْمَتِهِۦ, tr:ve izi'tezeltumûhum ve mâ ya'budûne illallâhe fe'vû ile'l-kehfi yenşur lekum rabbukum min rahmetih, gloss:madem onlardan ve Allah'tan başka taptıklarından ayrıldınız, mağaraya sığının ki Rabbiniz rahmetinden size yaysın, source:18:16}. Bu hikâyede asrın üç yüzü bir arada görünür, ama kelimenin kendisi geçmez: sığınak, uzun bir çağ ve uyuyanın bir an sandığı süre. Üçüncü ayette istisna edilen iman edenler bu sığınak imgesine yaslanır; kayıptan kurtuluş, bu sahnede bir yere sığınmak olarak duyulur.

## Kasırga ve kokunun yükselişi

[¶20] Kökün bir dalı göğe yükselen bir rüzgârı adlandırır. Rüzgâr yerden eser, tozu kaldırır ve onu sütun gibi göğe diker: {ar:الإعصار ريح تهب تثير الغبار فيرتفع إلى السماء كأنه عمود, tr:el-i'sâru rîhun tehubbu tusîru'l-gubâra fe-yertefi'u ile's-semâi keennehû amûd, gloss:i'sâr, esip tozu kaldıran ve onu sütun gibi göğe yükselten rüzgârdır, source:"ع ص ر,B004"}; dönerek yükselen tozun kendisine de {ar:الإعصار الغبار الذي يسطع مستديرا والجمع الأعاصير, tr:el-i'sâru'l-gubâru'llezî yesta'u mustedîrâ, gloss:i'sâr, dönerek yükselen tozdur, çoğulu eâsîr, source:"ع ص ر,B004"} denir. Bu rüzgârın işi, yerdeki şeyi döndürerek bir araya toplamak ve onu dik bir sütun hâlinde yukarı çekmektir. Aynı dal hoş bir şeyi de böyle anlatır: güzel kokular sürünmüş bir kadın geçtiğinde {ar:مرت امرأة متطيبة لذيلها عصر, tr:merrat imraetun mutetayyibetun li-zeylihâ asr, gloss:güzel koku sürünmüş bir kadın geçti, eteğinin ardından koku yükseliyordu, source:"ع ص ر,B004"} derlerdi; {ar:تكون العصرة من فوح الطيب وهيجه, tr:tekûnu'l-usratu min fevhi't-tîbi ve heycih, gloss:usra, kokunun yayılıp kabarmasıdır, source:"ع ص ر,B004"}. Hareket eden bir şeyin ardından kabarıp yükselen ya tozdur ya kokudur.

[¶21] Kur'an bu rüzgârı, yaşlılığın içine yerleştirilmiş bir bahçe misalinde anar. Allah Allah yolunda harcamaya dair misaller verir: gösteriş için harcayanın hâli üzerinde toprak bulunan düz bir kayadır, sağanak vurunca çıplak kalır {ar:فَمَثَلُهُۥ كَمَثَلِ صَفْوَانٍ عَلَيْهِ تُرَابٌۭ فَأَصَابَهُۥ وَابِلٌۭ فَتَرَكَهُۥ صَلْدًۭا, tr:fe-meseluhû ke-meseli safvânin aleyhi turâbun fe-esâbehû vâbilun fe-terakehû saldâ, gloss:onun misali, üstünde toprak olan düz bir kaya gibidir; sağanak vurdu, onu çıplak bıraktı, source:2:264}; Allah'ın rızası için harcayanınki ise sağanak da çisenti de alsa iki kat ürün veren tepedeki bir bahçedir {source:2:265}. Sonra bir soru gelir: {ar:أَيَوَدُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَن تَكُونَ لَهُۥ جَنَّةٌۭ مِّن نَّخِيلٍۢ وَأَعْنَابٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ, tr:e-yeveddu ehadukum en tekûne lehû cennetun min nahîlin ve a'nâbin tecrî min tahtihe'l-enhâr, gloss:biriniz, altından ırmaklar akan, hurmalık ve üzüm bağından bir bahçesi olmasını ister mi, source:2:266}; aynı ayette {ar:وَأَصَابَهُ ٱلْكِبَرُ وَلَهُۥ ذُرِّيَّةٌۭ ضُعَفَآءُ فَأَصَابَهَآ إِعْصَارٌۭ فِيهِ نَارٌۭ فَٱحْتَرَقَتْ, tr:ve esâbehu'l-kiberu ve lehû zurriyyetun duafâu fe-esâbehâ i'sârun fîhi nârun fahtarakat, gloss:kendisine yaşlılık çökmüş, zayıf çocukları varken, bahçeye içinde ateş olan bir kasırga isabet etsin de yansın, source:2:266}. Ayet kendi işini de söyler: {ar:كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ, tr:kezâlike yubeyyinullâhu lekumu'l-âyâti leallekum tetefekkerûn, gloss:Allah size ayetleri böyle açıklar ki düşünesiniz, source:2:266}.

[¶22] Bu bahçede kökün birkaç anlamı aynı yerde durur, ama kelime olarak yalnızca kasırga geçer. Bahçede üzüm vardır, yani sıkılacak meyve; ırmaklar ve bütün ürünler, yani gelir; sahibine yaşlılık gelmiştir, yani ömrün akşamüstü; ve bütün bunları, yerden kaldırdığını göğe diken, içinde ateş taşıyan bir rüzgâr yok eder. Bir ömür boyunca sıkılmayı bekleyen ürün, tam sahibinin yeniden ekecek gücü kalmadığı vakitte gider. İkinci ayetteki kaybın en somut resmi budur; kasırga, asrın yanında duyulduğunda zamanın biriktirdiğini bir anda savurabilen yüzüdür. Kokunun yükselişi ise aynı hareketin öteki ucunda durur: geçen birinin ardından toz değil, güzel bir iz kalabilir.

## ¶3
3a: Turkish has split the word: 'asır' now means century ('asri' contemporary) while the end of the day is 'ikindi', so the Turkish word loses the afternoon sense and the root's senses of pressing, refuge and whirlwind.  · terms: al-ʿaṣr
3b: The Qurʾānic word holds the hour and the age together, so that the end of a day and the end of a lifetime bear the same name.  · terms: ٱلْعَصْرِ, al-ʿaṣr  · verses: 103:1

## ¶4
4a: The Arabs used the dual al-ʿaṣrān for the two ends of the day: night and day (al-layl wa-l-nahār), or early morning and late afternoon (al-ghadāh wa-l-ʿashiyy).  · terms: العصران, al-ʿaṣrān, الغداة والعشي, al-ghadāh wa-l-ʿashiyy
4b: The phrase bi-l-ghadāti wa-l-ʿashiyy in 6:52 (the believers calling on their Lord morning and evening) is cited as the Qurʾān's own naming of the pair of day-ends that al-ʿaṣrān denotes.  · terms: بِٱلْغَدَوٰةِ وَٱلْعَشِىِّ, bi-l-ghadāti wa-l-ʿashiyy  · verses: 6:52
4c: The phrase ṭarafayi l-nahār in 11:114, giving the times of prayer, is cited as another Qurʾānic naming of the day's two ends, the pair called al-ʿaṣrān.  · terms: طَرَفَىِ ٱلنَّهَارِ, ṭarafayi l-nahār  · verses: 11:114
4d: That ʿaṣr names the two ends of the day shows the word grasps time at its edge, where a period is entered and left; the afternoon sense in 103:1 is one such edge, the closing end of the day.  · terms: العصران, al-ʿaṣrān, al-ʿaṣr  · verses: 103:1

## ¶5
5a: The root carries lateness: jāʾanī fulānun ʿaṣran means someone came late, slowly.  · terms: عصرا, ʿaṣran
5b: ʿAṣr also names a brief stretch, even a moment: nāma wa-mā nāma li-ʿaṣr (he lay down but did not sleep a moment) and al-ʿaṣār = al-ḥīn (a while); so ʿaṣr is both a long age and an instant.  · terms: نام وما نام لعصر, li-ʿaṣr, العصار الحين, al-ʿaṣār
5c: ʿAṣr names stages of a human life: of a girl, balaghat ʿaṣra shabābihā wa-idrākihā (she reached the age of youth and maturity), and a person's lifetime and old age are also called by this name.  · terms: بلغت عصر شبابها, ʿaṣr shabābihā
5d: The late-afternoon sense is read as time running short: the hour when least of the day remains and time narrows for what is undone, so that al-ʿaṣr is not only an hour but the lateness felt within it.  · terms: al-ʿaṣr, al-ʿashiyy  · verses: 103:1

## ¶6
6a: Lam yalbathū illā ʿashiyyatan aw ḍuḥāhā (79:46), answering the question about the Hour (79:42), is cited as the Qurʾān's instance of a whole lifetime shrinking, seen from the end, into one part of a day; the paragraph uses ʿashiyya, the afternoon by which ʿaṣr is glossed, to show how the long age and the afternoon held in al-ʿaṣr turn into each other from the end.  · terms: عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَىٰهَا, ʿashiyyatan aw ḍuḥāhā  · verses: 79:42, 79:46, 103:1
6b: The plea of the people of Hell in 35:37, rabbanā akhrijnā naʿmal ṣāliḥan, is cited as the Qurʾān's open instance of the work left too late, the lateness the paragraph hears in ʿaṣr.  · terms: نَعْمَلْ صَٰلِحًا, naʿmal ṣāliḥan  · verses: 35:37
6c: The reply in 35:37, a-wa-lam nuʿammirkum mā yatadhakkaru fīhi man tadhakkar, is read as naming life as an allotted span given for reflection; the loss of 103:2 and the faith and righteous deeds of 103:3 are placed within this given span, i.e. al-ʿaṣr is heard as the lifetime granted.  · terms: نُعَمِّرْكُم, nuʿammirkum  · verses: 35:37, 103:2

## ¶7
7a: The root's most concrete sense is pressing: ḍaghṭu shayʾin ḥattā yataḥallab, pressing a thing until its liquid flows out.  · terms: ضغط شيء حتى يتحلب, ḍaghṭ shayʾ ḥattā yataḥallab
7b: The images drawn from the pressing sense do not replace the sense of 'time' in 103:1 but are heard alongside it; the paragraph keeps time as the verse's meaning.  · terms: al-ʿaṣr  · verses: 103:1
7c: The vocabulary of pressing grapes: al-miʿṣār is a bag like a feed-bag in which grapes are pressed, al-maʿṣara the place of pressing, al-ʿuṣāra what flows from pressing, and ʿaṣīr anything whose juice has been pressed; the dregs remain in the bag.  · terms: المعصار, al-miʿṣār, المعصرة, al-maʿṣara, العصارة, al-ʿuṣāra, عصير, ʿaṣīr
7d: Pressing divides a thing in two: the essence that flows away and the dry mass left behind.  · terms: al-ʿaṣr

## ¶8
8a: The Arabs made al-ʿuṣāra and al-muʿtaṣar a figure for good and giving: of a generous man, yaʿṣiru fīnā ka-lladhī taʿṣir (he gives to us as you give), and al-ʿuṣāra also means al-ghalla, the yield of land.  · terms: العصارة والمعتصر, al-ʿuṣāra wa-l-muʿtaṣar, يعصر فينا, yaʿṣiru fīnā, العصارة الغلة, al-ʿuṣāra al-ghalla
8b: Pressing is carried to the sky: al-muʿṣirāt are clouds pressed with rain, saḥāba muʿṣir a cloud that yields rain as if milked, and ʿuṣira l-qawm means the people were rained upon.  · terms: المعصرات, al-muʿṣirāt, السحابة المعصر, al-saḥāba al-muʿṣir, عصر القوم, ʿuṣira l-qawm
8c: Al-muʿṣirāt in 78:14 (wa-anzalnā mina l-muʿṣirāti māʾan thajjājā) is taken as the rain clouds 'pressed' with rain, the Qurʾān naming these clouds with the root's word; other identifications of al-muʿṣirāt are not considered.  · terms: ٱلْمُعْصِرَٰتِ, al-muʿṣirāt  · verses: 78:14
8d: 78:14-16, addressed to those disputing the news of the Resurrection, are read as a chain of blessing set off by the pressing of clouds: pressed cloud, then grain, plants and dense gardens.  · terms: ٱلْمُعْصِرَٰتِ, al-muʿṣirāt, ثَجَّاجًۭا, thajjājā  · verses: 78:14, 78:15, 78:16

## ¶9
9a: The other end of pressing is dryness: al-maʿṣūr is the tongue dried out by thirst, a pressed tongue with no water left in it.  · terms: المعصور, al-maʿṣūr
9b: The same verb names a movement of rescue: al-iʿtiṣār is when one chokes on food and sips water little by little to get it down.  · terms: الاعتصار, al-iʿtiṣār
9c: The poet's verse law bi-ghayri l-māʾi ḥalqī shariqun kuntu ka-l-ghaṣṣāni bi-l-māʾi ʿtiṣārī is read as turning that image round: what chokes him is water itself, so no rescuing sip remains.  · terms: اعتصاري, iʿtiṣārī, كالغصان, ka-l-ghaṣṣān

## ¶10
10a: Heard beside the time of 103:1, these images show time as pressure: the days pass over a person and draw something out of him, either an essence that flows as gift, like rain from a cloud, or a dry mass like a thirst-dried tongue.  · terms: al-ʿaṣr  · verses: 103:1
10b: The loss (khusr) of 103:2 is read as the dry remainder of what has been pressed.  · terms: خُسْرٍ, khusr  · verses: 103:2
10c: Ṣabr, the last word of 103:3, is also the name of a bitter juice pressed from a tree (aloe), which carries the pressing image to the end of the sura.  · terms: الصبر, ṣabr

## ¶11
11a: Ḥattā ḥīn in 12:35 is read as measuring Joseph's imprisonment by a span of time, and linked to ʿaṣr meaning a stretch of time and also detention (al-ḥabs); the paragraph says this is a connection, not shared wording, since the Qurʾān uses another word (sijn) for the prison.  · terms: حَتَّىٰ حِينٍۢ, ḥattā ḥīn, al-ḥabs  · verses: 12:35
11b: In aʿṣiru khamran (12:36) what the youth presses is grapes, but the sentence names it by the drink that will come of it: pressing is named by its product.  · terms: أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًۭا, aʿṣiru khamran  · verses: 12:36
11c: Joseph's interpretation in 12:41 (fa-yasqī rabbahu khamran) is read as rescue for this youth, and 12:42 calls him the one who would be saved (nājin): the one who presses in his dream is the one who leaves the prison.  · terms: نَاجٍۢ, nājin, فَيَسْقِى رَبَّهُۥ خَمْرًۭا, fa-yasqī rabbahu khamran  · verses: 12:41, 12:42
11d: The lexical sense al-ʿaṣr = al-manjāh (place of rescue, escape) is heard echoing in this scene.  · terms: العصر المنجاة, al-ʿaṣr al-manjāh  · verses: 12:42

## ¶12
12a: In 12:42 it is the freed youth who forgets to mention Joseph to his master, and this forgetting prolongs Joseph's stay in prison by biḍʿa sinīn (some years).  · terms: فَلَبِثَ فِى ٱلسِّجْنِ بِضْعَ سِنِينَ, biḍʿa sinīn  · verses: 12:42
12b: Wa-ddakara baʿda umma in 12:45 is read as 'remembered after a long while' (umma as a span of time).  · terms: بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ, baʿda umma  · verses: 12:45
12c: Joseph's interpretation of the king's dream of seven green and seven dry ears (12:43) is read as a time plan: seven years of sowing with the harvest left in its ears (fa-dharūhu fī sunbulihi, 12:47), then seven hard years that eat what was stored except a little kept back (tuḥṣinūn, 12:48).  · terms: فِى سُنۢبُلِهِۦٓ, fī sunbulihi, تُحْصِنُونَ, tuḥṣinūn  · verses: 12:43, 12:47, 12:48
12d: When the sheaths of the ears appear, the Arabs said qad aʿṣara l-zarʿ, derived from al-ʿaṣr meaning al-ḥirz (protection) because the grain is guarded in its sheath; the paragraph links this to Joseph's plan of keeping grain in its ear, while noting the Qurʾān's word there is sunbul, not ʿaṣr.  · terms: عصر الزرع, aʿṣara l-zarʿ, العصر وهو الحرز, al-ʿaṣr al-ḥirz  · verses: 12:47
12e: Yaʿṣirūn in 12:49 is read as 'they press' (the year of relief in which pressing resumes) and is also reported as understood to mean 'they gain yield from their lands' (yastaghillūna bi-araḍīhim).  · terms: يَعْصِرُونَ, yaʿṣirūn, يستغلون بأرضيهم, yastaghillūna bi-araḍīhim  · verses: 12:49

## ¶13
13a: In the Joseph story the root's seemingly distant senses fall into one calendar: time spent in prison, pressing in the dream of the one to be rescued, forgotten and lengthening years, grain kept in its sheath, and the year of plenty when pressing begins again.  · terms: al-ʿaṣr  · verses: 12:35, 12:36, 12:42, 12:47, 12:49
13b: Pressing in this story marks the end of scarcity: the grapes to be pressed are the share of those who waited patiently through the hard years and stored.  · terms: يَعْصِرُونَ, yaʿṣirūn  · verses: 12:49
13c: Seen this way, the time sworn by in 103:1 is not only a span that consumes but one in which what is stored is protected and finally pressed out and flows.  · terms: ٱلْعَصْرِ, al-ʿaṣr  · verses: 103:1

## ¶14
14a: Al-ʿaṣr also means holding back: al-ʿaṣr = al-ḥabs, and mā ʿaṣaraka means 'what held you back, prevented you'.  · terms: العصر الحبس, al-ʿaṣr al-ḥabs, ما عصرك, mā ʿaṣaraka
14b: One who holds on and does not give is called ʿāṣir (= mumsik, tight-fisted).  · terms: عاصر, ʿāṣir
14c: The verb also names withholding and taking back property: yaʿtaṣiru l-wālidu ʿalā waladihi fī mālihi (the father withholds his child's property from him) and aʿṭaytu fulānan ʿaṭiyyatan fa-ʿtaṣartuhā (I gave a gift and then took it back).  · terms: يعتصر الوالد, yaʿtaṣiru l-wālid, فاعتصرتها, fa-ʿtaṣartuhā
14d: The same verb can name both open-handedness (the generous man who yaʿṣiru) and tight-fistedness, because both are gripping something in the hand; the difference is whether anything flows out of the grip.  · terms: يعصر, yaʿṣiru, عاصر, ʿāṣir

## ¶15
15a: Al-muʿṣir is a girl at the time of her first menstruation, so called because she is kept in the house and given a shelter (ʿaṣr); the grain kept in its sheath is within the same kind of shelter.  · terms: المعصر, al-muʿṣir
15b: Holding is not always blameworthy: here it means protecting one who stands at a threshold.  · terms: العصر الحبس, al-ʿaṣr al-ḥabs

## ¶16
16a: The story of the owners of the garden (68:17-27), who swore to harvest at dawn and meant to keep every poor person out (68:24), is cited as the Qurʾān's instance of what withholding produce brings: the withheld harvest did not stay in the withholders' hands (68:19-20, 68:26-27).  · terms: أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ, aṣḥāb al-janna, مِسْكِينٌۭ, miskīn  · verses: 68:17, 68:19, 68:20, 68:24, 68:26, 68:27
16b: Wa-lā yastathnūn (68:18) is read as 'they made no exception' in their oath.  · terms: وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ, wa-lā yastathnūn  · verses: 68:18
16c: Fa-aṣbaḥat ka-l-ṣarīm (68:20) is read as the garden turning out at morning cut down and black.  · terms: كَٱلصَّرِيمِ, ka-l-ṣarīm  · verses: 68:20
16d: The garden owners swore an oath without exception, whereas the sura's oath is completed by the general ruling of 103:2 followed by the exception (illā) of 103:3.  · terms: وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ, wa-lā yastathnūn  · verses: 68:17, 68:18, 103:2

## ¶17
17a: The root denotes clinging: taʿalluq bi-shayʾ wa-imtisāk bihi (hanging on to a thing and holding it tight), and the place clung to is called al-ʿaṣr = al-maljaʾ (refuge); iʿtaṣartu bi-fulān / taʿaṣṣartu means I took refuge with someone, and iʿtaṣara bi-l-makān he took refuge in a place.  · terms: العصر الملجأ, al-ʿaṣr al-maljaʾ, اعتصرت بفلان, iʿtaṣartu bi-fulān, تعصرت, taʿaṣṣartu
17b: The idiom ʿuṣrat al-manjūd ties this refuge to the hard-pressed: the refuge of one in distress.  · terms: عصرة المنجود, ʿuṣrat al-manjūd
17c: The bond between two people is named by the word through its absence: mā baynahumā ʿaṣrun wa-lā yaṣr, there is neither affection nor kinship between them.  · terms: ما بينهما عصر ولا يصر, mā baynahumā ʿaṣr wa-lā yaṣr
17d: Al-ʿunṣur (root, lineage) is said to come from al-ʿaṣr in the sense of refuge, with an added nūn: one's lineage is where one turns for refuge.  · terms: العنصر, al-ʿunṣur
17e: Al-maʿāṣir, coats of mail, are said to derive from al-ʿaṣr because one is protected by them.  · terms: المعاصر, al-maʿāṣir

## ¶18
18a: That one word names both squeezing and refuge is only an apparent contradiction: both are a grip. Pressing wraps a thing from outside, the one taking refuge grips something tightly, armour wraps and protects the body; the hard-pressed run to refuge, as the idiom ʿuṣrat al-manjūd says.  · terms: عصرة المنجود, ʿuṣrat al-manjūd, al-ʿaṣr al-maljaʾ
18b: Heard beside the time of 103:1, this image makes the time sworn by both a span that presses man and a place of refuge.  · terms: ٱلْعَصْرِ, al-ʿaṣr  · verses: 103:1

## ¶19
19a: The youths' taking refuge in the cave (fa-ʾwū ilā l-kahf, 18:16; idh awā l-fityatu ilā l-kahf, 18:10) and their sleep (fa-ḍarabnā ʿalā ādhānihim, 18:11) are cited as the Qurʾān's instance of a refuge that closes time off.  · terms: فَأْوُۥٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ, fa-ʾwū ilā l-kahf, أَوَى, awā, فَضَرَبْنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ, fa-ḍarabnā ʿalā ādhānihim  · verses: 18:10, 18:11, 18:16
19b: The sleepers' estimate labithnā yawman aw baʿḍa yawm (18:19) is set against wa-labithū fī kahfihim thalātha miʾatin sinīna wa-zdādū tisʿā (18:25), which the paragraph takes as the true length of their stay.  · terms: لَبِثْنَا يَوْمًا أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍۢ, labithnā yawman aw baʿḍa yawm, ثَلَٰثَ مِا۟ئَةٍۢ سِنِينَ وَٱزْدَادُوا۟ تِسْعًۭا, thalātha miʾatin sinīna wa-zdādū tisʿā  · verses: 18:19, 18:25
19c: The Cave story shows three faces of ʿaṣr together, refuge, a long age, and the span the sleeper takes for a moment, though the word itself does not occur there.  · terms: al-ʿaṣr  · verses: 18:10, 18:19, 18:25
19d: The believers excepted in 103:3 lean on this refuge image: deliverance from loss is heard as taking refuge.

## ¶20
20a: Al-iʿṣār is a wind that blows, raises dust and lifts it to the sky like a column, and also the dust that rises in a spiral (plural aʿāṣīr): a wind that gathers what is on the ground by turning it and draws it up as an upright column.  · terms: الإعصار, al-iʿṣār, الأعاصير, al-aʿāṣīr
20b: The same branch describes rising scent: of a perfumed woman passing, li-dhaylihā ʿaṣar (scent rises behind her train), and al-ʿuṣra is the wafting and stirring of perfume.  · terms: لذيلها عصر, li-dhaylihā ʿaṣar, العصرة, al-ʿuṣra
20c: What links whirlwind and scent is a single motion: what swells and rises behind a moving thing is either dust or fragrance.  · terms: الإعصار, al-iʿṣār, العصرة, al-ʿuṣra

## ¶21
21a: Iʿṣārun fīhi nārun fa-ḥtaraqat in 2:266 is cited as the Qurʾān's use of the iʿṣār whirlwind, set in a parable of a garden whose owner has reached old age with weak children.  · terms: إِعْصَارٌۭ فِيهِ نَارٌۭ, iʿṣārun fīhi nār  · verses: 2:266
21b: The 2:266 parable is read in the series of parables on spending in God's way: after 2:264 (spending for show, like soil on a smooth rock washed bare by a downpour) and 2:265 (spending for God's pleasure, a hillside garden yielding double), and closing with kadhālika yubayyinu llāhu lakumu l-āyāti laʿallakum tatafakkarūn.  · terms: صَفْوَانٍ, ṣafwān, أَيَوَدُّ أَحَدُكُمْ, a-yawaddu aḥadukum  · verses: 2:264, 2:265, 2:266

## ¶22
22a: In the 2:266 garden several senses of the root stand together though only iʿṣār occurs as a word: grapes (aʿnāb, fruit to be pressed), rivers and all produce (yield), old age (al-kibar) as the afternoon of a life, and the fiery whirlwind that destroys it all.  · terms: أَعْنَابٍۢ, aʿnāb, ٱلْكِبَرُ, al-kibar, إِعْصَارٌۭ, iʿṣār  · verses: 2:266
22b: The produce awaited a lifetime is lost just when its owner has no strength left to plant again; this is read as the most concrete picture of the loss (khusr) of 103:2.  · terms: خُسْرٍ, khusr, ٱلْكِبَرُ, al-kibar  · verses: 2:266, 103:2
22c: Heard beside al-ʿaṣr, the whirlwind is the face of time that can scatter in a moment what time has accumulated.  · terms: إِعْصَارٌۭ, iʿṣār, ٱلْعَصْرِ, al-ʿaṣr  · verses: 103:1, 2:266
22d: The rising of scent stands at the other end of the same motion: behind one who passes, a fragrant trace rather than dust may remain.  · terms: العصرة, al-ʿuṣra

#8 IBNJAWZI-ZAD d.597 · الحسن ومجاهد وأبو صالح · reports · “Establishing themselves” means carefully considering where to place their expenditure. «أنه التثبيت لارتياد محل الإنفاق فهم ينظرون أين يضعونها»
#9 IBNJAWZI-ZAD d.597 · holds · Janna means a garden; Mujahid and Asim al-Jahdari read ḥabba instead. «الجنة البستان وقرأ مجاهد وعاصم الجحدري حبة بالحاء»
#10 IBNJAWZI-ZAD d.597 · ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي · reports · These readers pronounce rabwa with a ḍamma on the rāʾ. «وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي بربوة بضم الراء»
#11 IBNJAWZI-ZAD d.597 · عاصم وابن عامر · reports · They pronounce rabwa with a fatḥa on the rāʾ. «وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر بفتح الراء»
#12 IBNJAWZI-ZAD d.597 · الحسن والأعمش · reports · They pronounce the rāʾ in rabwa with a kasra. «وقرأ الحسن والأعمش بكسر الراء»
#13 IBNJAWZI-ZAD d.597 · ابن عباس وأبو رزين · reports · They read rabāwa with an added alif and a fatḥa; Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Asim al-Jahdari add the alif but use a ḍamma, and variants occur in al-Mu'minun too. «وقرأ ابن عباس وأبو رزين برباوة بزيادة ألف وفتح الراء»
#14 IBNJAWZI-ZAD d.597 · الزجاج · reports · Rabwa has three vowel variants and denotes high land with enough water, which yields more than low ground. «يقال ربوة وربوة وربوة ورباوة والموضع المرتفع من الأرض إذا كان له ما يرويه»
#15 IBNJAWZI-ZAD d.597 · ابن كثير ونافع · reports · They read akulaha with a light, unvowelled kāf everywhere; Abu Amr agrees when the word is attached to a feminine noun, while Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i always use the heavier form. «قرأ ابن كثير ونافع أكلها والأكل بسكون الكاف حيث وقع»
#16 IBNJAWZI-ZAD d.597 · holds · Akul means fruit, and du'fin means twofold. «وأكلها أي ثمرها ﴿ ضعفين ﴾ أي مثلين»
#17 IBNJAWZI-ZAD d.597 · ابن قتيبة · reports · Tall means weaker rain. «فأما الظل فقال ابن قتيبة هو أضعف المطر»
#18 IBNJAWZI-ZAD d.597 · الزجاج · reports · Tall is continuous, fine rain with small drops that scarcely make water channels run. «هو المطر الدائم الصغار القطر الذي لا تكاد تسيل منه المثاعب»
#19 IBNJAWZI-ZAD d.597 · holds · The future form describes a past possibility: if no downpour struck, a light drizzle did; the garden owner and sincere believer are not disappointed by either rain. «وهذا لفظ مستقبل وهو لأمر ماض فمعناه فإن لم يكن أصابها وابل فطل»
#20 IBNJAWZI-ZAD d.597 · holds · The garden prospers under light rain or a downpour, just as a sincere believer's giving bears fruit in either case. «فكذلك نفقة المؤمن المخلص»
#21 IBNJAWZI-ZAD d.597 · الخطابي · reports · Basir means the One who sees; its form fa'il functions like the active participle muf'il. «والبصير من أسماء الله تعالى معناه المبصر قال الخطابي وهو فعيل بمعنى مفعل»
#22 RAZI-FULL d.606 · holds · The contrasting sincere donors spend for two ends: seeking God's pleasure and تثبيت of themselves. «غرض هؤلاء المنفقين من هذا الانفاق أمران»
#23 RAZI-FULL d.606 · القفال · reports · Al-Qaffāl offers a seed analogy: sincere deeds grow like seed in fertile garden soil, while the reproacher's deed is seed stored on sterile stone and yields nothing when needed. «قال القفال رحمه الله تعالى ، وفيه احتمال آخر» [filed under 2:264, 2:265]
#24 RAZI-FULL d.606 · holds · Repeated giving for God's pleasure creates a lasting disposition: even an accidental lapse quickly returns the heart toward the sacred, spiritually aligning the person with angelic and holy realities. «صيرورة هذا الابتغاء والطلب ملكة مستقرة في النفس»
#25 RAZI-FULL d.606 · الزجاج · reports · Al-Zajjāj says تثبيت is confident assurance that God will not waste or disappoint the donors' work, unlike the hypocrite who sees giving as wasted without belief in reward. «قال الزجاج : المراد من التثبيت أنهم ينفقونها»
#26 RAZI-FULL d.606 · الحسن ومجاهد وعطاء · reports · Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, and ʿAṭāʾ interpret تثبيت as careful placement of alms among people of integrity; al-Ḥasan says a donor gives when the motive is truly for God. «قال الحسن ومجاهد وعطاء : المراد أن المنفق»
#27 RAZI-FULL d.606 · holds · The word ربوة means elevated, swelling ground; the author favors fertile soil that rises and grows with rain over interpreters' ordinary hill, citing Q 22:5 and the contrast with sterile stone. «وأصلها من قولهم : ربا الشيء يربو إذا ازداد وارتفع»
#28 RAZI-FULL d.606 · عاصم وابن عامر · reports · ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read ربوة with fatḥa on rāʾ, a Tamīm dialect; the other readers use ḍamma, the more common Qurashī form, among seven variants. «قرأ عاصم وابن عامر { بربوة } بفتح الراء»
#29 RAZI-FULL d.606 · القاضي · reports · Al-Qāḍī says تثبيت means training oneself to preserve obedience and avoid what corrupts it, including subsequent reproach and injury. «يوطنون أنفسهم على حفظ هذه الطاعة وترك ما يفسدها»
#30 RAZI-FULL d.606 · مجاهد · reports · Mujāhid's reading, وتثبيتا من بعض أنفسهم, supports construing تثبيت as reassuring others that the donors' faith and sincerity are genuine. «ويعضده قراءة مجاهد { وتثبيتا من * بعض * أنفسهم }»
#31 RAZI-FULL d.606 · صاحب الكشاف · reports · The Kashshāf explains that struggle subdues part of the self attached to worldly life and wealth; spending money stabilizes part, while spending life stabilizes all, as in al-Ṣaff 61:11. «ومعشوقها أمران : الحياة العاجلة والمال»
#32 RAZI-FULL d.606 · holds · Al-Rāzī proposes that the heart becomes firm through God's remembrance; spending brings calm only when done solely for worship, illustrated by ʿAlī's words in al-Insān 76:9. «أن ثبات القلب لا يحصل إلا بذكر الله»
#33 RAZI-FULL d.606 · reports · He also cites the report about Abū Bakr's spending as seeking only God's face, and notes the rational principle that repeating acts produces stable dispositions. «ووصف إنفاق أبي بكر فقال»
#34 RAZI-FULL d.606 · المفسرون · rejects · Exegetes say a garden on a hill yields better, but al-Rāzī objects that elevation or a valley each has disadvantages and prefers fertile swelling soil, supported by Q 22:5 and the stone contrast. «البستان إذا كان في ربوة من الأرض كان أحسن وأكثر ريعا»
#35 RAZI-FULL d.606 · ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو · reports · Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, and Abū ʿAmr lighten أكلها; the remaining readers intensify it. The word means edible fruit or produce, as in Ibrāhīm 14:25, with lexical poetry cited. «قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو { أكلها } بالتخفيف»
#36 RAZI-FULL d.606 · الزجاج · reports · Al-Zajjāj reads ضعفين as twice as much; ʿAṭāʾ says a single year's yield equals another garden's two-year yield, while al-Aṣamm and Abū Muslim give related doubled-yield readings. «قال الزجاج : { اتت أكلها * ضعفين } يعني مثلين»
#37 RAZI-FULL d.606 · holds · Ṭall is light rain. Either a fertile garden preserves its full yield despite receiving only light rain, or it still yields some fruit; sincere giving is never wasted, little or much. «الطل : مطر صغير الفطر»
#38 RAZI-FULL d.606 · holds · God sees the amount and manner of spending and its motives, then recompenses each person accordingly, for good with good and evil with evil. «هو تعالى عالم بكمية النفقات وكيفيتها»
#39 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · A rabwa is a slightly elevated place, usually with deep soil and better growth, which explains why it is chosen for the parable. «والربوة: المكان المرتفع ارتفاعا يسيرا، معه في الأغلب كثافة تراب»
#40 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن عطية · rejects · Ibn Atiyya rejects al-Tabari's identification with the 'gardens of al-Ḥazn': those are the gardens of Najd, whose growth and air he says are superior to Tihama's. «قال ابن عطية: ورياض الحزن ليست من هذا كما زعم الطبري، بل تلك هي الرياض المنسوبة إلى نجد»
#41 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · reports · An Arab woman compared her husband to a Tihama night, invoked as evidence that Tihama's air is unpleasant except at night. «وقلما يصلح هواء تهامة إلا بالليل ولذلك قالت الأعرابية:»
#42 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · السدي · reports · Al-Suddi reads rabwa as rabāwa, a low-lying place; Ibn Atiyya calls the wording awkward, and the author says it is untenable because the root means increase and elevation. «وقال السدى: «بربوة» أي برباوة، وهو ما انخفض من الأرض»
#43 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · الفراء · reports · Al-Farra explains 'a severe seizure' in 69:10 as increased and compares it with taking more than one gave, as evidence for the root's sense of increase. «وقال الفراء في قوله تعالى:»

#44 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · الخليل · reports · Al-Khalil defines rabwa as elevated, good land; the author says the verse pictures a raised place without running water, familiar from Arab experience. «وقال الخليل: الربوة أرض مرتفعة طيبة وخص الله تعالى بالذكر»
#45 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن عباس · reports · Ibn Abbas defines rabwa as elevated land without rivers, inferred from the verse's rainfall; it cannot mean only river-fed land because 11:98 mentions a rabwa with stable water and a spring. «وقال ابن عباس: الربوة المكان المرتفع الذي لا تجري فيه الأنهار»
#46 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · In common Arabic, rabwa means any land raised above its surroundings, whether or not water flows there. «والمعروف من كلام العرب أن الربوة ما ارتفع عما جاوره سواء جرى فيها ماء أو لم يجر»
#47 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · reports · The first four readings are ḍamma for Ibn Kathir, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, Nafi, and Abu Amr; fatḥa for Asim, Ibn Amir, and al-Hasan; kasra for Ibn Abbas and Abu Ishaq; and rabāwa with fatḥa for Abu Jaʿfar and Abu Abd al-Rahman. «وفيها خمس لغات «ربوة» بضم الراء، وبها قرأ ابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي ونافع وأبو عمرو»
#48 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · Aṣābah refers to the elevated ground; wābil is heavy rain, and the cited poem describes a luxuriant garden watered by a downpour. «يعني الربوة. { وابل } أي مطر شديد قال الشاعر:»
#49 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · rejects · Some propose inverted word order, making the garden yield after either heavy rain or drizzle; the author prefers the ordinary order and sees no need for inversion. «قلت: التأويل الأول أصوب ولا حاجة إلى التقديم والتأخير»
#50 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · The parable depicts sincere spending growing as God nurtures charity, like a foal or young camel, unlike dust washed off a bare rock. «فشبه تعالى نمو نفقات هؤلاء المخلصين الذين يربي الله صدقاتهم كتربية الفلو والفصيل»
#51 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · الفراء · reports · Al-Ashhab al-Uqayli reads rabāwa with kasra; al-Farra records rabāwa variants and derives them from rising, from rabā yarbū. ««رباوة» بالكسر، وبها قرأ الأشهب العقيلي. قال الفراء: ويقال برباوة»
#52 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · Ātāt means 'yielded'; ukul is edible fruit, with 14:25 as a parallel; ukla can also mean a bite or two, as in a Muslim report. «أي أعطت. { أكلها } بضم الهمزة»
#53 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · The possessive link to the garden is one of association, like a horse's saddle or a house's door, since the garden itself does not eat fruit. «وإضافته إلى الجنة إضافة اختاص، كسرج الفرس وباب الدار»
#54 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · نافع · reports · Nafi, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read ukul with a ḍamma on hamza and a still kāf in feminine possessives; Abu Amr lengthens other contexts where the others lighten, while Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i lengthen all listed forms. «وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو «أكلها» بضم الهمزة وسكون الكاف،»
#55 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · Akl and ukl mean the same thing. «ويقال: أكل وأكل بمعنى»
#56 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · prefers · The garden yields twice the fruit of other land; the author prefers this over the report that it bears twice yearly, meaning one year's yield equals two years elsewhere. «أي أعطت ضعفي ثمر غيرها من الأرضين»
#57 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · المبرد · reports · Al-Mubarrad supplies an omitted phrase: if no downpour reaches it, a light rain is enough; al-Zajjaj instead glosses the phrase as the light rain that reaches it. «قال المبرد وغيره: تقديره فطل يكفيها. وقال الزجاج: فالذي يصيبها طل»
#58 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن عباس · reports · Al-Tall is light, fine rain according to Ibn Abbas and others; Mujahid and some others identify it with dew, which Ibn Atiyya calls figurative comparison. «والطل: المطر الضعيف المستدق من القطر الخفيف قاله ابن عباس وغيره»
#59 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · الماوردي · reports · Al-Mawardi notes that dew-fed crops yield less than rain-fed crops but retain some growth and benefit. «قال الماوردي: وزرع الطل أضعف من زرع المطر وأقل ريعا، وفيه وإن قل»
#60 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · رسول الله · reports · Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that God takes a single date from lawful earnings and nurtures it like a colt or young camel until it becomes mountain-sized or greater; Muslim and the Muwatta transmit it. «لا يتصدق أحد بتمرة من كسب طيب إلا أخذها الله بيمينه»
#61 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · God's seeing what people do conveys both promise and warning. «قوله تعالى: { والله بما تعملون بصير } وعد ووعيد»
#62 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · الزهري · reports · Al-Zuhri reads 'they do' in the third person; the pronoun may refer to people generally or just donors, in which case the statement is pure promise. «وقرأ الزهري «يعملون» بالياء كأنه يريد به الناس أجمع،»
#63 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · Ibtighāʾ is parsed as a purpose complement and tathbītan coordinated with it; Makki treats both as purpose complements, but Ibn Atiyya rejects that analysis for tathbītan because spending is not done for the sake of stabilization. «قال مكي في المشكل: كلاهما مفعول من أجله. قال ابن عطية: وهو مردود»
#64 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · النحاس · reports · Al-Nahhas says Mujahid's interpretation would require tathabbatan; Qatada's 'expecting reward' is unfamiliar unless it means that their souls, expecting reward, strengthen them, which he finds far-fetched. «وقال النحاس: لو كان كما قال مجاهد لكان وتثبتا من تثبت»
#65 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · النحاس · prefers · Al-Nahhas approves al-Sha'bi's sense: one's own certainty strengthens resolve and judgment to spend in obedience to God. «وقول الشعبي حسن، أي تثبيتا من أنفسهم لهم على إنفاق ذلك»
#66 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · reports · Another explanation is that donors acknowledge God will confirm the reward, unlike a hypocrite who does not expect recompense. «وقيل: «وتثبيتا من أنفسهم» أي يقرون بأن الله تعالى يثبت عليها»
#67 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · A janna is an orchard, a plot whose trees cover it; the word shares the root of jinn and embryo because they are hidden. «الجنة: البستان، وهي قطعة أرض تنبت فيها الأشجار حتى تغطيها»
#68 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن عطية · prefers · Ibn Atiyya says ibtighāʾ is best read as a verbal noun functioning circumstantially, coordinated with the verbal noun tathbītan; purpose accusative remains possible for ibtighāʾ alone. ««ابتغاء» نصب على المصدر في موضع الحال»
#69 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · After warning against corrupt charity, the passage now describes spending that flourishes because it follows the law and its proper intent. «ولما ذكر الله تعالى صفة صدقات القوم الذين لا خلاق لصدقاتهم»
#70 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · Ibtighāʾ means seeking, and marḍāt is the verbal noun of raḍiya. ««ابتغاء» معناه طلب. و «مرضات» مصدر من رضي يرضى»
#71 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · مجاهد · reports · Mujahid and al-Hasan interpret tathbītan as carefully considering where to place charity; al-Hasan describes giving only after confirming the motive is God's. ««وتثبيتا» معناه أنهم يتثبتون أين يضعون صدقاتهم قاله مجاهد والحسن»
#72 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن عباس · reports · Ibn Abbas explains tathbītan as belief and certainty; he and Qatada also explain it as seeking God's reward. «وقيل: معناه تصديقا ويقينا قاله ابن عباس. وقال ابن عباس أيضا وقتادة: معناه واحتسابا»
#73 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · الشعبي · reports · Al-Sha'bi, al-Suddi, Qatada, Ibn Zayd, Abu Salih, and others understand tathbītan as certainty: insightful souls strengthen a person to spend in obedience. «وقال الشعبي والسدي وقتادة أيضا وابن زيد وأبو صالح وغيرهم: «وتثبيتا» معناه وتيقنا»
#74 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن عطية · prefers · Ibn Atiyya prefers the certainty, reward-seeking, and confirmation readings over al-Hasan and Mujahid because the latter give the verbal noun a nonliteral sense without an explicit preceding verb. «وهذه الأقوال الثلاث أصوب من قول الحسن ومجاهد لأن المعنى الذي ذهبا إليه»
#75 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن عطية · reports · Ibn Atiyya says a verbal noun used in a different sense requires an explicit antecedent verb, as in 71:17 and 73:8. «قال ابن عطية: وهذا لا يسوغ إلا مع ذكر المصدر والإفصاح بالفعل المتقدم»
#76 BAYDAWI-FULL d.685 · reports · Tathbit min anfusihim may mean strengthening part of themselves in faith, since wealth is kin to the soul and giving wealth steadies part of oneself while giving wealth and life steadies all of it. «ابتغاء مرضات الله وتثبيتا من أنفسهم } وتثبيتا بعض أنفسهم على الإيمان»
#77 BAYDAWI-FULL d.685 · reports · Alternatively, it means confirming Islam and confidence in recompense from the core of themselves; spending purifies the donor from miserliness and love of wealth. «أو تصديقا للإسلام وتحقيقا للجزاء مبتدأ من أصل أنفسهم»
#78 BAYDAWI-FULL d.685 · holds · The elevated garden represents charity, especially zakat; its height improves its appearance and fruit. «أي ومثل نفقة هؤلاء في الزكاة، كمثل بستان بموضع مرتفع»
#79 BAYDAWI-FULL d.685 · holds · Ibn Amir and Asim read rabwah with fatḥa; a kasra reading is also reported, and all three vowel forms are dialect variants. «وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم { بربوة } بالفتح وقرىء بالكسر وثلاثتها لغات فيها.»
#80 BAYDAWI-FULL d.685 · holds · Ibn Kathir, Nafi, and Abu Amr read akl with sukūn as a lightened form; the crop yields twice its usual amount after heavy rain. «{ فأتت أكلها } ثمرتها. وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو بالسكون للتخفيف.»
#81 BAYDAWI-FULL d.685 · reports · Du'fayn means twice as much, with du'f meaning a like amount; another view takes it as four times the yield. «{ ضعفين } مثلي ما كنت تثمر بسبب الوابل. والمراد بالضعف المثل كما أريد بالزوج الواحد»
#82 BAYDAWI-FULL d.685 · holds · The accusative is circumstantial, meaning multiplied; if no heavy rain falls, light rain suffices because of the garden's rich soil and cool elevated air. «{ فإن لم يصبها وابل فطل } أي فيصيبها، أو فالذي يصيبها طل، أو فطل يكفيها»
#83 BAYDAWI-FULL d.685 · holds · The parable says sincere donations are accepted and never lost, though their value varies with accompanying circumstances; the garden can represent their standing with God and heavy or light rain their greater or lesser donations. «أن نفقات هؤلاء زاكية عند الله لا تضيع بحال وإن كانت تتفاوت»

#85 NASAFI-FULL d.710 · holds · Seeking God's approval and تثبيت mean affirming Islam and truly believing in recompense from within oneself; spending evidences sincere faith in reward. «أى وتصديقا للاسلام وتحقيقا للجزاء من أصل أنفسهم»
#86 NASAFI-FULL d.710 · holds · Min marks the origin of تثبيت, coordinated with the purpose of spending; the likeness concerns the standing of their purified expenditure with God. «ومن لابتداء الغاية وهو معطوف على المفعول له»
#87 NASAFI-FULL d.710 · holds · A garden on high ground is especially apt because its trees produce purer and better fruit. «وخصها لأن الشجر فيها أزكى وأحسن ثمرا»
#88 NASAFI-FULL d.710 · عاصم والشامي · reports · They read the word for high ground as rabwa. «بربوة عاصم وشامى»
#89 NASAFI-FULL d.710 · نافع ومكي وأبو عمرو · reports · Their reading gives the word for its produce the vocalization recorded in the source. «ثمرتها أكلها نافع ومكى و أبو عمرو ﴿ ضعفين ﴾ مثلى ما كانت تثمر»
#90 NASAFI-FULL d.710 · holds · A downpour makes the garden yield twice its previous crop; even a light drizzle suffices because of the excellence of its soil. «مثلى ما كانت تثمر قبل بسبب الوابل ﴿ فإن لم يصبها وابل فطل ﴾ فمطر صغير القطر»
#91 NASAFI-FULL d.710 · holds · The garden and its rains portray the spenders' large or small expenditures: either is pure and increases their nearness and good standing with God when done for His approval. «وكما أن كل واحد من المطرين يضعف أكل الجنة فكذلك نفقتهم كثيرة كانت أو قليلة»
#92 NASAFI-FULL d.710 · holds · God sees both the amount spent and the intentions behind it, including any ostentation. «يرى أعمالكم على إكثار وإقلال ويعلم نياتكم فيهما من رياء»
#93 QASHANI d.736 · holds · The second kind of spending is superior to the first: a garden continues bearing fruit unlike a grain, signifying enduring possession as an acquired quality. «فضله على الأول بتشبيهه بالجنة، فإن الجنة مع إيتاء أكلها تبقى بحالها»
#94 QASHANI d.736 · holds · Giving stabilizes the soul in generosity, a divine attribute; the hill signals higher rank, and abundant or light rain signifies abundant or smaller shares of mercy. «توطينا لها على الجود الذي هو صفة ربانية»
#95 QASHANI d.736 · holds · God sees the acts and knows which category of giving they belong to. «بأعمالكم يرى أنها من أي القبيل»
#96 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الخليل · reports · Al-Khalīl defines ربوة as elevated, fertile land; the word also has variant forms and a cited poem describes rain over its slopes. «الربوة: قال الخليل: أرض مرتفعة طيبة،»
#97 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الأخفش · reports · Al-Akhfash prefers ḍamma in ربوة because the plural الربا is commonly heard; the source rejects al-Suddī’s interpretation as low-lying land and connects the root with increase and height. «وقال الأخفش: ويختار الضم في ربوة لأنه لا يكاد يسمع في الجمع إلا الربا،»
#98 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · مجاهد · reports · Most lexicographers define طل as very light rain; Mujāhid and others extend it metaphorically to dew, and a cited poem mentions dew on a dwelling. «الطل: المستدق من القطر الخفيف، هذا مشهور اللغة. وقال قوم، منهم مجاهد:»
#99 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The fertile-garden parable contrasts the showy unbeliever with sincere spenders; ابتغاء مرضات الله answers رئاء الناس, while تثبيتا answers lack of faith by describing resolve to preserve the gift from corruption, grounded in certainty of the afterlife. «ذكر ضده بتمثيل محسوس للذهن»
#100 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The same three omitted-subject patterns used for the seed parable apply here: the hypocrites may be likened to a planter, their spending to a seed, or spenders and spending together to seed and planter. «والتقادير الثلاثة التي في قوله: مثل الذين ينفقون أموالهم في سبيل الله كمثل حبة جارية هنا،»
#101 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ابن عطية · reports · Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects taking ابتغاء as a purpose-object because it coordinates with تثبيتا, and says spending is not done for تثبيت; Makkī calls both purpose complements, which Abū Ḥayyān also rejects. «قال ابن عطية: ولا يصح أن يكون ابتغاء مفعولا من أجله،»
#102 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · ابتغاء and تثبيتا may be circumstantial nouns or purpose complements; تثبيتا is a transitive verbal noun whose omitted object may be God’s reward, making its acquisition a motive for giving. «وتثبيت، مصدر: ثبت، وهو متعد، ويحتمل أن يكون المفعول محذوفا»
#103 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الشعبي، وقتادة، والسدي، وأبو صالح، وابن زيد · reports · These authorities interpret تثبيتا as certainty: deeply grounded insight strengthens the self to give; Qatāda also explains it as expecting reward, and an anomalous reading تبيينا is cited as support. «قال الشعبي، وقتادة، والسدي، وأبو صالح، وابن زيد: معناه وتيقنا،»
#104 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الشعبي والضحاك والكلبي · reports · They gloss تثبيتا as giving zakat while being content with the act. «وقال الشعبي أيضا والضحاك، والكلبي: وتصديقا، أي: يخرجون الزكاة طيبة بها أنفسهم»
#105 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · He reads the verse as spenders steadying their faith through a difficult act, which humbles the self and makes it yield. «أنهم يثبتون من أنفسهم على الإيمان بهذا العمل»
#106 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · When the strengthening is attributed to the spenders, min is partitive and governed by the verbal noun; when attributed to the selves, it describes the source of strengthening. «وإذا كان التثبيت مسندا إليهم كانت: من، في موضع نصب متعلقة بنفس المصدر»
#107 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الزمخشري · reports · Al-Zamakhshari raises the question of what the partitive min means. «قال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: فما معنى التبعيض»
#108 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ابن جبير وأبو مالك · reports · They understand تثبيتا as confirmation in their religion. «وقال ابن جبير، وأبو مالك: تحقيقا في دينهم»
#109 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ابن كيسان · reports · He explains it as sincerity and strengthening themselves in obedience through their spending. «وقال ابن كيسان: إخلاصا وتوطيدا لأنفسهم على طاعة الله في نفقاتهم»
#110 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الزجاج · reports · He says spenders believe their giving is something for which God will reward them. «وقال الزجاج: ومقرين حين ينفقون أنها مما يثيب الله عليها»
#111 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الشعبي · reports · He also glosses تثبيتا as resolve. «وقال الشعبي أيضا: عزما»
#112 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · يمان · reports · He also glosses تثبيتا as insight. «وقال يمان أيضا: بصيرة»
#113 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · مجاهد والحسن · reports · They take تثبيتا to mean that the spenders strengthen themselves; Hasan describes pausing before charity and giving only when it is truly for God. «وقال مجاهد، والحسن: معناه أنهم يثبتون، أي يضعون صدقاتهم»
#114 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · rejects · He rejects an Egyptian proposal that تثبيتا means intransitive تثبتا: an unmentioned verbal noun cannot be assigned another verb's original construction. «ورد هذا القول بأن ذلك لا يكون بالفعل المتقدم على المصدر نحو الآية»
#115 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The author distinguishes intransitive ثبت, meaning to become firm, from causative ثبّت, meaning to make firm or establish. «إن ثبت فعل لازم معناه: تمكن، ورسخ، وتحقق. وثبت معدى بالتضعيف»
#116 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الزمخشري · reports · He says spending for God steadies part of oneself, while giving both wealth and life in God's path steadies all of it. «ومن بذل ماله وروحه معا فهو الذي ثبتها كلها»
#117 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The garden parable contrasts with the first parable: the stone does not benefit from rain. «وأنه في مقابلة المثل الأول، والأول لا يؤثر فيه المطر، وهو: الصفوان»
#118 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The self itself moves and steadies the giver through its faith and expectation of abundant reward. «والظاهر أن نفسه هي التي تثبته وتحمله على الإنفاق في سبيل الله»
#119 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The high ground is singled out for its good trees and abundant fruit. «وخص الربوة لحسن شجرها وزكاء ثمرها»
#120 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الخليل بن أحمد · reports · His poem depicts a raised garden between dry heights and thirsty lowlands, watered by itself and bearing fruit at different levels. «كما قال الشاعر، وهو الخليل بن أحمد»
#121 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ابن عباس · reports · He explains rabwa as elevated land without flowing rivers; the author limits this to the particular garden because it receives rain. «وتفسير ابن عباس: الربوة، بالمكان المرتفع الذي لا يجري فيه الأنهار»
#122 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The garden depends on rain rather than running water, as was familiar in Arabia. «وخصت بأن سقياها الوابل لا الماء الجاري فيها على عادة بلاد العرب»
#123 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الرازي · reports · He objects that gardens on high ground lack river water and face winds, while hollows collect water; he instead reads rabwa as fertile earth swelling under rain. «فالمراد بالربوة ليس ما ذكروه، وإنما هو كون الأرض طيبة»
#124 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الحسن · reports · Hasan had already explained rabwa as level ground that does not rise above the water. «وما قاله قاله قبله الحسن. الربوة الأرض المستوية التي لا تعلو فوق الماء»
#125 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · rejects · He rejects al-Tabari's interpretation of رياض الحزن as gardens of elevated ground; it means gardens of Najd, called al-Hazn. «ولا يراد: برياض الحزن، رياض الربا، كما زعم الطبري»
#126 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · rejects · Ḍiʿfayn is a circumstantial accusative, not a second object; taking آتت to mean produced with one object lacks support in Arabic usage. «ونصب: ضعفين، على الحال، ومن زعم أن: ضعفين، مفعول ثان»
#127 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · Fruit is attached to the garden by relation, not ownership; al-ḥamza in الأكل marks the thing eaten. «والأكل بضم الهمزة الشيء المأكول، وأريد هنا الثمر»
#128 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الحرميان وأبو عمرو · reports · They read ukul with ḍamma on hamza and sukūn on kāf in the described feminine annexation contexts; Abu Amr also transmits a distinction by annexed noun. «وقرأ الحرميان، وأبو عمرو بضم الهمزة، وإسكان الكاف»

#129 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The remaining readers use the heavier vocalization for ukul. «والباقون بالتثقيل»
#130 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · Najd's gardens are praised because their vegetation is more fragrant and their air cooler and finer than Tihama's. «لأن نباته أعطر، ونسيمه أبرد، وأرق. فهي خير من رياض تهامة»
#131 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ابن عامر وعاصم · reports · They read rabwa with fatḥa on rāʾ, while the other five canonical readers use ḍamma; the same difference occurs at قد أفلح. «وقرأ ابن عامر، وعاصم بفتح الراء، وباقي السبعة بالضم»
#132 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ابن عباس · reports · He reads rabwa with kasra on rāʾ. «وقرأ ابن عباس بكسر الراء»
#133 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الرحمن · reports · They read برباوة on the pattern of كراهة. «وقرأ أبو جعفر، وأبو عبد الرحمن: برباوة، على وزن: كراهة»
#134 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · أبو الأشهب العقيلي · reports · He reads برباوة on the pattern of رسالة. «وأبو الأشهب العقيلي: برباوة، على وزن رسالة»
#135 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · أصابها وابل is an adjectival clause for garden, following the fixed location description; it may instead be a circumstantial clause. «أصابها وابل جملة في موضع الصفة لجنة»
#136 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The wording first gives the lasting feature of being on a high place, then the incidental event of rain; its ordering differs from the stone parable. «وبدىء بالوصف الثابت، وهو: كونها بربوة، ثم بالوصف العارض»
#137 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · آتت means gave, with its recipient omitted; the first object is owner or people and أكل means the edible fruit. «آتت بمعنى: أعطت، والمفعول الأول محذوف، التقدير: فآتت صاحبها»
#138 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · reports · Ḍiʿfayn may mean twice the normal yield because of rain and the high place, twice other land, or fourfold if a double is taken as two times. «وقيل: ضعفي غيرها من الأرضين، وقيل: أربعة أمثالها»
#139 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الزمخشري · reports · He compares sincere spenders to the garden, and abundant or modest spending to heavy rain or dew; either is accepted when seeking God's face and exerting one's capacity. «فكما أن كل واحد من المطرين يضعف أكل الجنة، فكذلك نفقتهم كثيرة»
#140 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · أبو مسلم · reports · He says the garden yields three times as much; Taj al-Qurra rejects this as having no basis in Arabic and says the doubled yield is one harvest. «وقال أبو مسلم: ثلاثة أمثالها»
#141 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · عكرمة وعطاء · reports · They interpret doubled fruit as two harvests in one year. «وقال عكرمة، وعطاء: معنى ضعفين أنها حملت في السنة مرتين»
#142 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · prefers · He suggests ḍiʿfayn can express multiplication rather than exactly twice one yield, meaning many successive multiples, matching the manyfold reward for good deeds. «بل يكون من التشبيه الذي يقصد به التكثير»
#143 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ابن عيسى · reports · He supplies an omitted clause after the conditional: if rain does not strike it, as in the poetic example where لم تلدني means she did not happen to bear me. «قال ابن عيسى: فيه إضمار، التقدير: فإن لم يكن يصيبها وابل»
#144 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · reports · On one reading, dew substitutes for heavy rain and the fertile land still yields doubled fruit despite less rainfall. «والمعنى: أن الطل يكفيها وينوب مناب الوابل في إخراج الثمرة ضعفين»
#145 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الماوردي · reports · Alternatively, dew yields less than heavy rain, but still gives some yield and benefit. «قال الماوردي: زرع الطل أضعف من زرع المطر وأقل ريعا»
#146 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · rejects · He rejects proposed fronting and postponement as unnecessary and says the Qur'an should not be assigned a poetic license. «لا حاجة إليها. والتقديم والتأخير من ضرورات الشعر، فينزه القرآن عن ذلك»
#147 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · زيد بن أسلم · reports · He identifies the parable's land as Egypt, which thrives without rain and doubles its yield with rain. «قال زيد بن أسلم: المضروب به المثل أرض مصر»
#148 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الماوردي · reports · He compares abundant charity to rain-fed crops and modest charity to dew-fed crops, so a little good should not be abandoned when one cannot give much. «فلا يدع قليل البر إذا لم يفعل كثيره»
#149 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ابن عطية · reports · He compares the growth of sincere gifts, which God nurtures like young livestock, to vegetation on the fertile raised garden, unlike bare stone. «شبه نمو نفقات هؤلاء المخلصين الذين يربي الله صدقاتهم»
#150 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ابن الجوزي · reports · He says the sincere believer's expenditure never fails: dew makes the garden good and heavy rain doubles it. «معنى الآية أن صاحب هذه الجنة لا يخيب»
#151 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · He parses فطل as the conditional answer with an omitted clause, offering several viable ellipses; the simplest remove one part of a clause. «وقوله: فطل، جواب للشرط، فيحتاج إلى تقدير بحيث تصير جملة»
#152 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · A present verb after fa requires an implicit subject, as in the cited verse, so that analysis also needs an omitted clause. «متى دخلت الفاء على المضارع فإنما هو على إضمار مبتدأ»
#153 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · reports · A poetic parallel uses a verbless noun phrase after the condition, like the parsing of فطل. «ألا إن لا تكن إبل فمعزى»
#154 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الزهري · reports · He reads بصير with yāʾ, apparently referring to hypocrites, though the author allows a general reference to everyone. «قرأ الزهري، بالياء، فظاهره أن الضمير يعود على المنافقين»
#155 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The majority read بصير with address to the audience; the shift of address highlights that God knows every deed and intention, promising reward and warning. «وقرأ الجمهور بالتاء، على الخطاب، وفيه التفات»
#156 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · أبو البقاء · reports · تثبيتا can be the verbal noun of intransitive تثبت, used in place of التثبت; verbal nouns substitute for one another, as in 73:8, and a reading تثبتا supports this. «أن التثبيت مصدر تثبت فهو واقع موقع التثبت، والمصادر تنوب عن بعضها.»
#157 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · ابن رواحة · reports · Ibn Rawāḥa’s line uses تثبيت with ثبت الله and supports the transitive verb’s verbal-noun usage. «قال ابن رواحة: 1067 فثبت الله ما أتاك من حسن تثبيت عيسى»
#158 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الشيخ · rejects · Al-Shaykh rejects substitution unless the corresponding verb is explicitly stated first; otherwise a verbal noun keeps its original verb’s meaning. «ورد هذا القول بأن ذلك لا يكون إلا مع الإفصاح بالفعل المتقدم على المصدر،»
#159 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الشيخ · holds · He instead distinguishes intransitive ثبت, ‘become firm,’ from causative ثبّت, ‘make firm.’ «والذي نقول: إن ثبت - يعني مخففا - فعل لازم معناه تمكن ورسخ، وثبت معدى بالتضعيف،»
#160 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الزمخشري · reports · Al-Zamakhsharī explains partitive من as partial self-commitment: spending wealth steadies part of oneself, while giving life and wealth steadies the whole self. «معناه أن من بذل ماله لوجه الله فقد ثبت بعض نفسه»
#161 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الشيخ · prefers · The apparent meaning is that believers’ own faith steadies and moves them to spend; the author therefore favors construing تثبيت as attributed in meaning to themselves. «والظاهر أن نفسه هي التي تثبته وتحمله على الإنفاق في سبيل الله»
#162 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · If تثبيت is attributed to the spenders, من is an accusative partitive attached to the verbal noun; if attributed semantically to themselves, من also modifies تثبيتا. «فإذا كان التثبيت مسندا إليهم كانت " من " في موضع نصب متعلقة بنفس المصدر،»
#163 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الخليل · reports · ربوة is an elevated, fertile tract, derived from ربا يربو, ‘rise’; al-Suddī’s interpretation as low-lying land is wrong. «والربوة: أرض مرتفعة طيبة، قاله الخليل. وهي مشتقة من ربا يربو أي: ارتفع،»
#164 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · Forms include ربوة and رباوة with three vowelings, plus رابية; the cited poem witnesses روابيه. «ويقال: ربوة ورباوة بتثليث الراء فيهما، ويقال أيضا: رابية، قال:»
#165 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · ابن عامر وعاصم · reports · Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read ربوة with fatḥa; the others use ḍamma. «وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم " ربوة " بالفتح، والباقون الضم،»
#166 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الأخفش · prefers · Al-Akhfash prefers ḍamma because the plural رباً points to a singular with ḍamma, like برمة/برم and صورة/صور. «قال الأخفش: " ونختار الضم لأنه لا يكاد يسمع في الجمع إلا الربا "»
#167 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · ابن عباس · reports · Ibn ʿAbbās reads ربوة with kasra. «وقرأ ابن عباس " ربوة " بالكسر،»
#168 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الأشهب العقيلي وأبو جعفر · reports · Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī reads رياوة and Abū Jaʿfar reads رباوة, alongside other dialect forms. «والأشهب العقيلي: " رياوة " ، مثل رسالة وأبو جعفر: " رباوة " مثل كراهة،»
#169 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · prefers · أصابها وابل may be a second adjective of جنة; preferred order puts the stable location before the temporary rain event and commonly places a prepositional phrase before a clause. «أحدها: أنها صفة ثانية لجنة، وبدىء هنا بالوصف بالجار والمجرور ثم بالجملة،»
#170 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · أبو البقاء · reports · It may instead modify ربوة, since the garden is part of the elevated tract. «أن تكون صفة ل " ربوة " ، قال أبو البقاء: " لأن الجنة بعض الربوة "»
#171 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · A third analysis makes the clause circumstantial from the implicit pronoun inside the prepositional phrase describing the garden. «أن تكون حالا من الضمير المستكن في الجار لوقوعه صفة.»
#172 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · A fourth analysis makes it circumstantial from جنة, now specified by its adjective, with قد understood. «أن تكون حالا من " جنة " ، وجاز ذلك لأن النكرة قد تخصصت بالوصف،»
#173 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · prefers · آتت normally takes two objects, with صاحبها or أهلها omitted as first because the point is what the garden yields and its owner is implied; أكلها is second and ضعفين circumstantial. «وهو الأصح أن " آتت " تتعدى لاثنين، حذف أولهما وهو " صاحبها " أو " أهلها ".»
#174 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · rejects · Treating ضعفين as the second object is a slip and an error. «والثاني: أن " ضعفين " هو المفعول الثاني، وهذا سهو من قائله وغلط.»
